findings.title: Hardcoded AWS access keys committed in provider, EC2 user-data, and Lambda env
findings.attack_path: Static keys AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE / secret appear in providers.tf, ec2.tf user_data, and lambda.tf environment. Anyone with repo or state access (or who reads instance user-data via IMDS) lifts the credentials and authenticates directly to the AWS API, bypassing all network controls.
findings.remediation: Remove all literal keys; use the default credential provider chain, instance roles, and Secrets Manager. Rotate the exposed keys and add secret scanning (git-secrets/trufflehog) to CI.

findings.title: Public S3 bucket 'data' holding customer-master.xlsx with no encryption/logging/versioning
findings.attack_path: The 'data' bucket is commented as public and stores customer-master.xlsx. An unauthenticated attacker enumerates the predictable bucket name (account-acme-dev-data) and downloads the customer spreadsheet; absence of access logs means the read is untraceable.
findings.remediation: Set Block Public Access at bucket and account level, apply aws:kms SSE, enable versioning and server access logging, and scope the bucket policy to least privilege.

findings.title: Security group exposes SSH (22) and HTTP (80) to 0.0.0.0/0
findings.attack_path: web-node SG opens port 22 and 80 to the entire internet. An attacker scans the public IP, brute-forces or exploits SSH, and gains a shell on web_host/db_app, then pivots using the attached instance role.
findings.remediation: Restrict SSH ingress to a bastion or VPN CIDR (or use SSM Session Manager), and front HTTP with the load balancer / WAF instead of exposing instances directly.

findings.title: RDS MySQL instance publicly accessible, unencrypted, weak hardcoded password, no backups
findings.attack_path: aws_db_instance.default sets publicly_accessible=true, storage_encrypted=false, backup_retention_period=0, username=admin and a default password (Aa1234321Bb). The endpoint is reachable from the internet on 3306; an attacker connects with the known credentials and reads/destroys the database with no backup to recover.
findings.remediation: Set publicly_accessible=false, enable storage_encrypted, set a strong secret-managed password, enable backups and deletion protection, and restrict the SG to the app tier only.

findings.title: Over-permissive IAM: instance role and IAM user grant wildcard service actions on all resources
findings.attack_path: ec2role policy allows s3:*/ec2:*/rds:* on Resource * and the IAM user excess_policy allows ec2:*/s3:*/lambda:*/cloudwatch:* on *. Any compromise of an instance (via IMDS) or of the user's access key yields near-administrative control and account-wide lateral movement.
findings.remediation: Replace wildcards with least-privilege actions scoped to specific ARNs, require IMDSv2, and prefer short-lived roles over long-lived IAM user access keys.

findings.title: Sensitive data stores at rest left unencrypted (S3 financials/operations/data_science, EBS, Neptune, Aurora)
findings.attack_path: The financials/operations/data_science buckets, the web_host EBS volume and its snapshot, the Neptune cluster (storage_encrypted=false), and the Aurora clusters have no at-rest encryption. An attacker who obtains a snapshot, volume, or storage-layer access reads plaintext data, and the unencrypted snapshot can be shared cross-account.
findings.remediation: Enable SSE-KMS on all S3 buckets, encrypted=true on EBS volumes/snapshots, storage_encrypted=true on Neptune and Aurora, and restrict snapshot sharing.

findings.title: Elasticsearch domain access policy allows es:* to any AWS principal
findings.attack_path: aws_elasticsearch_domain_policy grants actions es:* with Principal AWS:* on resource *. Combined with no VPC/IP restriction and an end-of-life ES 2.3 engine, an external principal can read and modify the monitoring index.
findings.remediation: Scope the access policy to specific principals and source IP/VPC, deploy the domain inside the VPC, enable node-to-node and at-rest encryption, and upgrade off the unsupported 2.3 engine.

findings.title: Classic ELB and EC2 web tier serve plaintext HTTP (no TLS)
findings.attack_path: The ELB listens on HTTP :80 to instance :8000 and the web servers serve plain HTTP. A network-positioned attacker observes or modifies traffic (including the employee form data) in transit; no HTTPS listener or certificate is configured.
findings.remediation: Add an HTTPS listener with an ACM certificate, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, and enforce TLS end to end (or migrate to ALB/NLB with TLS).

findings.title: EKS cluster control-plane endpoint allows public access by default
findings.attack_path: The eks_cluster vpc_config sets endpoint_private_access=true but does not disable public access, so the API server remains reachable from the internet. Nodes run in public subnets (map_public_ip_on_launch). An attacker reaching the public endpoint can attempt API auth abuse and, on success, schedule workloads across the cluster.
findings.remediation: Set endpoint_public_access=false (or restrict public_access_cidrs), place nodes in private subnets, enable control-plane logging, and enable secrets envelope encryption.

findings.title: Unrestricted egress (0.0.0.0/0) enables data exfiltration from the VPC tier
findings.attack_path: The RDS/default security group and the web-node SG allow all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised instance or database host can freely beacon to attacker infrastructure and exfiltrate data over any protocol.
findings.remediation: Restrict egress to required destinations/ports, route outbound through a controlled NAT/proxy, and add egress monitoring.

findings.title: Workloads auto-assigned public IPs in public subnets (broad internet exposure)
findings.attack_path: web_subnet and web_subnet2 set map_public_ip_on_launch=true behind an internet gateway, so every instance (web_host, db_app) gets a routable public IP. This maximizes the externally reachable attack surface for the other findings.
findings.remediation: Disable map_public_ip_on_launch for application subnets, place workloads in private subnets, and expose only the load balancer publicly.

findings.title: Secrets and sensitive endpoints exposed via Terraform outputs and remote state
findings.attack_path: Outputs expose db_endpoint, the EC2/DB public DNS, and the IAM user secret; the password, keys, and access key material are stored in the Terraform state in the S3 backend. Anyone with read access to state or output logs harvests live secrets and target endpoints.
findings.remediation: Mark secret outputs sensitive, avoid emitting credentials at all, lock down the state bucket (encryption, versioning, least-privilege, no public access), and store secrets in Secrets Manager referenced at runtime.

findings.title: Provisioned PHP application accepts user input with weak query construction
findings.attack_path: db_app user_data writes an index.php that takes $_POST['NAME']/$_POST['ADDRESS'] and runs string-built mysqli queries against the RDS admin account. Any weakening of the escaping (or the SELECT * employee listing path) exposes the public app to injection and data tampering using a high-privilege DB user.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized/prepared statements, connect with a least-privilege DB user instead of admin, and front the app with a WAF; do not bake application source into instance user-data.

findings.title: ECR repository uses mutable tags and unscanned image; build pulls public base image
findings.attack_path: image_tag_mutability=MUTABLE with no scan_on_push, and the Dockerfile pulls python:3.7-slim (EOL) from Docker Hub. An attacker who can push to the repo or compromise the upstream base image overwrites an existing tag, and downstream pulls run the tampered image.
findings.remediation: Set image_tag_mutability=IMMUTABLE, enable scan_on_push, pin base images by digest, and use a controlled internal registry mirror.
